properties.note: Galilee as Josephus bounds it (Jewish War 3.3.1): Ptolemais's territory and Mount Carmel to the west, Samaria and Scythopolis to the south, the Jordan and the lake to the east, and Tyre's country to the north. Josephus says Carmel 'had formerly belonged to the Galileans, but now belonged to the Tyrians'. The edges are approximate. The line runs through the eastern end of Carmel, through Ginea and Scythopolis, and includes the north-east Jordan strip from this project's Herodian-area build where Josephus gives no exact line. It takes the western half of the Sea of Galilee.
Extracted whole from crete-cyrene part 0; Cauda is excluded.

Cyrenaica, 'the parts of Libya around Cyrene' (Acts 2:10), as this project's AD 69 area draws it. Its west edge meets the coast of the Great Syrtis 158 km east of the Euphrantas Tower (Euphranta, modern Sirte), which Strabo gives as the boundary 'as it was under Ptolemy' (17.3.20), and 79 km west of the Altars of the Philaeni, which Strabo and Pliny (5.4) name at the head of the gulf. No source this project cites gives the first-century line, so the west, desert and east edges are approximate.
Extracted whole from sicily part 1 (Malta only; Mljet remains the low-confidence candidate).

Samaria, which Josephus says 'begins at a village...called Ginea, and ends at the Acrabbene toparchy' (Jewish War 3.3.4). Its south edge runs through Anouath Borkeos, 'the northern boundary of Judea' (3.3.5), and north of Akraba (Acrabatta), a toparchy that both Josephus and Pliny count in Judea; between those places the line is approximate. The coast is split with Judea on that line as a convention: Josephus gives Judea's breadth from the Jordan to Joppa and says its maritime places reach Ptolemais, while Pliny calls the coast from Ascalon to Caesarea 'the region of Samaria' but lists Joppa among Judea's toparchies (Natural History 5.14-15).

Judea as Josephus describes it (Jewish War 3.3.5), with Idumea, which he counts among Judea's portions; Pliny counts Idumea separately (Natural History 5.14–15). Its north edge, shared with Samaria, runs through Anouath Borkeos and north of Akraba (Acrabatta), and is approximate. The coast is split with Samaria along that line, a convention neither author states: Josephus gives Judea's breadth from the Jordan to Joppa and says its maritime places reach Ptolemais, while Pliny calls the coast from Ascalon to Caesarea 'the region of Samaria' but lists Joppa among Judea's toparchies (5.14–15). The coast from Raphia to Rhinocolura is left out: Pliny places those towns and Gaza in Idumaea and Palaestina, and Josephus says Augustus added Gaza to Syria (Antiquities 17.11.4). The districts of Gaza and of Ascalon, which Pliny calls a free town, aren't drawn separately and lie inside this outline.

The kingdom of Pontus, including Pontus Galaticus and Lesser Armenia as this project's Pontus area draws them, since no source draws a line between these lands, plus the coast east of the lower Halys with Amisus and Themiscyra (Strabo 12.3.9; ISBE, 'Pontus'). The west cut follows Natural Earth's Kızılırmak line from the 35.621°E, 41.287°N tripoint downstream; one short straight segment ties the tripoint to the first river vertex, and a second runs north to the sea where the river line ends.

Pisidia as Strabo and ISBE place it between the Taurus front above Pamphylia and the Phrygian valleys (Strabo 12.7.1–2; ISBE, 'Pisidia'), bounded by Lycia/Milyas on the west and Isauria on the east. Antioch-near-Pisidia is kept outside by the project's M5-19 convention, while Pliny 5.24 places Antioch inside Pisidia; this outline follows the Strabo/ISBE reading and names Pliny's alternative.

Lycaonia as Strabo's upland plain east of Iconium and bounded by Cappadocia, Pisidia/Phrygia and Cilicia Tracheia (Strabo 12.6.1–3; ISBE, 'Lycaonia'), with the south clipped to exclude this project's drawn Cilicia areas (PO-3/R52). Iconium is kept outside per M5-19 ruling P5, though Strabo 12.6.1 and Pliny 5.25 place it in Lycaonia; both readings are disputed. Lake Tatta is left in neither Lycaonia nor Phrygia (PO-3).

Mysia as the mainland region from Olympene to the Caicus/Pergamene country (Strabo 12.8.1, 12.8.12), clipped to the Asian mainland (PO-6/R53): no Thrace and no Lesbos. Elaea is kept inside following Strabo's Caicus reading, while Pliny 5.32 treats it in Aeolis; this is disputed and noted. Cadi is treated on Phrygia's side where a single-point shared boundary is not explicit (PO-5).

Phrygia as the trans-provincial region Strabo and ISBE describe across Asian and Galatian Phrygia (Strabo 12.8.13–17; ISBE, 'Phrygia'), with Iconium inside per M5-19 ruling P5. Carura is treated as an outside anchor fallback where a through-point shared line is not explicit (Strabo 12.8.16; R23/A12). Strabo and Pliny disagree on several compass placements and on Cadi's side; this outline follows the project's PO rulings and keeps confidence low.

Media including Atropatene as Strabo 11.13 and ISBE describe it, with Rhagae kept inside (PO-2). The north-west follows the Aras→Kura chain to the Artaxata→Gazaca segment (PO-7/R50), then closes by the Artaxata/Gazaca equidistant construction against Armenia. The east and south remain equidistant constructions from sourced anchors against Parthia/Persis/Susiana. Gazaca's site and Rhagae's side are disputed in the sources and are named here.

Mesopotamia between the Euphrates and Tigris (Strabo 16.1.21–23, 28), closed in the south from Babylon to Seleucia (PO-8). The north line is an equidistant construction from Edessa/Carrhae/Nisibis against Arsamosata (R54–R57), so that edge is low confidence and is shown with Strabo's Zeugma-based reading noted as the alternative.
